questions.stem: Mary, 26, is in your GP clinic with 2 days of constant left calf pain and swelling. She takes the combined pill. While examining her, you tell the examiner you will check for calf swelling, which is one of the Wells score criteria. How should you measure it?
options: Measure both calves 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity and compare the two
Measure the left calf at its widest point and compare it with the expected norm
Measure both legs 10 cm above the medial malleolus and compare the two
Measure both thighs 15 cm above the upper pole of the patella and compare
questions.why: In the Wells score, calf swelling counts only if the symptomatic calf is more than 3 cm bigger than the other leg, measured 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity on both sides. Mary's 3.5 cm difference scores 1 point.
notes: Wells compares one leg with the patient's other leg, not with a population norm, and the 'widest point' is a different spot on each leg, so the two measurements can't be compared.
This measures the lower leg near the ankle, not the calf. Ankle oedema is assessed as pitting oedema, which is a separate Wells item.
Thigh swelling isn't the calf criterion. 'Entire leg swollen' is a separate Wells item, and Mary's thighs were equal.

questions.stem: Mary, 26, has an ultrasound-confirmed acute left popliteal DVT that extends into her calf veins. She has no features of PE, her observations are normal, she is not pregnant, and her FBC, clotting and renal and liver function are normal (CrCl about 145 mL/min). You plan to treat her as an outpatient. Which anticoagulant regimen should she start today?
options: Rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily with food from day 1, continued for 3 months
Apixaban 5 mg twice daily from day 1, continued for 3 months
Rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily with food for 21 days, then 20 mg daily with food
Warfarin 5 mg daily alone, adjusted to keep the INR between 2 and 3
questions.why: Acute VTE treated with a DOAC needs a higher-dose loading phase first. For rivaroxaban this is 15 mg twice daily for 21 days, then 20 mg daily, taken with food. Treat for 3 months for a provoked DVT, then review.
notes: This is the maintenance dose. If you skip the 21-day loading phase at 15 mg twice daily, the dose is too low in the early weeks, when the risk of recurrence is highest.
This is apixaban's maintenance dose. Initial treatment needs 10 mg twice daily for 7 days first.
Warfarin alone isn't used to start treatment. It takes days to work and can briefly make clotting more likely, so it needs heparin overlap until the INR is 2 to 3.

questions.stem: Mary, 26, has taken a combined oestrogen-containing oral contraceptive pill for 8 years and now has an acute left popliteal DVT. She has no personal or family history of VTE. By which mechanism does the oestrogen in her pill mainly raise her risk of venous thrombosis?
options: It raises the platelet count by stimulating hepatic thrombopoietin release
It damages the venous endothelium directly, exposing subendothelial collagen
It inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, which lowers protein C activity
It raises hepatic synthesis of clotting factors and lowers natural anticoagulants
questions.why: Oestrogen acts on the liver. It increases production of procoagulant factors (fibrinogen and factors II, VII, VIII and X) and reduces protein S and antithrombin, which causes acquired resistance to activated protein C. This makes the blood more likely to clot, the hypercoagulability part of Virchow's triad.
notes: The combined pill does not cause a clinically meaningful thrombocytosis, and Mary's platelet count is normal.
Direct injury to the vessel wall is the endothelial part of Virchow's triad, as seen in trauma or surgery. It is not how oestrogen causes thrombosis.
Inhibiting vitamin K epoxide reductase is how warfarin works. Oestrogen does not do this.

questions.stem: Mary's ultrasound shows occlusive thrombus in her left popliteal vein, while the femoral and common femoral veins above it are compressible and clot-free. You explain that the clot stops at the popliteal vein, before the vein continues as the femoral vein. At which landmark does the popliteal vein become the femoral vein?
options: The lower border of the popliteus muscle
The saphenous opening of the fascia lata
The adductor hiatus in adductor magnus
questions.why: The popliteal vein passes upwards through the adductor hiatus, a gap in the adductor magnus tendon, and from there it is called the femoral vein. Clot in the popliteal vein or above it counts as a proximal DVT.
notes: This is where the popliteal vein begins: the anterior and posterior tibial veins join here. It isn't where the popliteal vein ends.
Here the common femoral vein becomes the external iliac vein, which is much higher than the popliteal–femoral junction.
Here the great saphenous vein joins the femoral vein, in the upper thigh. It isn't where the popliteal vein ends.
